title: Hyperbolic-Tangent Shocks in a Lossy Nonlinear Transmission Line
abstract: We investigate traveling fronts in a lossy nonlinear transmission line. By prescribing a hyperbolic-tangent profile with dimensionless width $m$, we solve the inverse problem of determining the voltage--charge relation for which this profile is an exact solution. The exact relation is expressed in terms of the Gauss hypergeometric function. We also construct an approximate solution by assuming a cubic voltage--charge relation and replacing the resulting quadratic damping function with its optimal linear least-squares approximation. This construction determines the cubic coefficients and yields a modified governing equation that admits the prescribed profile as an exact solution. In both constructions, physical admissibility selects a shock front. In the broad-front limit, the approximate normalized force agrees with the exact result through order $m^{-2}$; numerical comparisons show that the agreement remains good even outside the asymptotic region of large $m$. Finally, a characteristic analysis of the original partial differential equations distinguishes compressive shocks from noncompressive kinks without recourse to the mechanical analogy.
summary: This paper investigates traveling shock fronts in a lossy nonlinear transmission line by solving an inverse problem for the required voltage-charge relation. The authors derive both exact and approximate solutions, demonstrating that physical constraints select a shock front. The work rigorously distinguishes between shocks and kinks using characteristic analysis of the underlying partial differential equations.
main_problem: The paper solves an inverse problem to determine the voltage-charge relation required for a specific hyperbolic-tangent traveling front profile in a lossy nonlinear transmission line.
main_result: Both exact and approximate constructions confirm that physical admissibility selects a shock front, and the results show asymptotic agreement up to order m^-2 in the broad-front limit.
method: The authors employed an inverse problem approach by prescribing the $	anh$ profile, alongside constructing an approximation assuming a cubic voltage-charge relation and using characteristic analysis on the underlying PDEs.
model_or_system: The system is a lossy nonlinear transmission line modeled by coupled partial differential equations. The dynamics are reduced to an ODE for traveling waves, characterized by nonlinearity and damping terms.
key_observables: Normalized force $eF(v)$, the distinction between compressive shocks (Lax-type) and noncompressive kinks via characteristic analysis, and the voltage-charge relation expressed using the Gauss hypergeometric function.
important_parameters: Dimensionless width parameter ($m$), dimensionless squared wave speed ($w$), and the front velocity $U$.
main_assumptions: The exact solution is found by prescribing a $	anh$ profile. The approximation assumes a cubic voltage-charge relation, and the analysis relies on continuum approximations of discrete unit cells.
figures_summary: Figures compare the exact normalized force $eF(v)$ with the least-squares approximation $e_{FG}(v)$ across various parameters ($m$ and $w$), illustrating asymptotic agreement.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by setting up the PDE model, solving the inverse problem exactly to find the required voltage-charge relation (involving ${}_2F_1$), developing an approximate solution via cubic fitting, and finally using characteristic analysis to rigorously distinguish between shock and kink solutions.
why_interesting: While not directly quantum mechanical, the mathematical techniques used—solving nonlinear PDEs, inverse problem formulation, and analyzing wave front structures (shocks/kinks)—are highly relevant to understanding non-equilibrium dynamics in open quantum systems or classical field theories derived from quantum models.
